estimator: 5-fold episode-grouped cross-fit (fold seed 0) of L2 logistic regression (C=1, standardised on the fit fold); score = AUC of the out-of-fold P(decel). Delta-AUC CI: EPISODE-RESAMPLING bootstrap (B=2000, seed 0) -- draw the episodes with replacement, recompute AUC(B)-AUC(A) on the resampled windows with the out-of-fold predictions held FIXED, 2.5/97.5 percentiles. NOT taniteval.ci (a paired bootstrap of per-episode deltas is invalid for an AUC). Answers: would another draw of EPISODES say this? -- it is blind to training-run and to inference-run variance (the models here are convex, so the former is nil).

lead_features.frame_convention: join agents are in the EGO frame of their own frame (+x forward, +y left); the lead is the nearest centre (smallest cx) with 0 < cx <= 80 m and |cy| <= 1.8 m at the NOW frame ws (= the window origin t0; refc_v3_train.py:4635 lookup(eid, t + w - 1)); all join classes count (automobile, truck, bus, person, rider, ...), occluded or not (GT upper bound)

pose_free_consistency.reading: world-frame lead speed (ego poses) vs v0 + Euclidean range rate; they differ by the ego speed change over the past second

real_control_lead_vs_ego_1s_travel.definition: windows in the GT-cruise population with v0 > 10 m/s and GT displacement at +1 s > 10 m (the ego keeps cruising at > 10 m/s): count windows with a lead whose range cx < the ego's GT 1 s travel (a lead inside the distance the ego covers in the next second while the ego keeps cruising is physically implausible); NOT filtered on

extra_closer_cases_are_followers.reading: all of them are short-gap following (time gap < 1 s, lead speed ~ ego speed) -- compatible with the GT ego cruising; a misaligned join or pose would instead give leads at ego-frame positions the GT path drives through at a closing speed
